tagline: Good answers start with a better question
intro: We are a research studio for consumer brands. You bring the question your team keeps circling; we find the people who can answer it, measure what can be measured and tell you plainly what we found.
audience: Founders and marketing leads at US direct-to-consumer brands in food, beauty, home and wellness, usually between their first retail listing and their first national campaign.
pricing_note: Each project is a fixed price, quoted after a free thirty-minute call. Small questions start as a two-week sprint; bigger ones are split into stages you approve one at a time.

services.title: Market sizing
services.description: How many people could buy what you sell, how often and at what price, built from survey data and public sources, with the assumptions spelled out.

services.title: Competitor teardowns
services.description: We buy, unbox, subscribe and cancel with your closest rivals, then compare their pricing, promises and customer experience with yours.

services.title: Customer interviews
services.description: One-to-one conversations with buyers, lapsed buyers and people who almost bought, so you learn what tipped them in or out.

services.title: Surveys that get answered
services.description: Short, well-written surveys sent to the right panel, with results cut by the segments you care about and written up in plain English.

process.title: Sharpen the question
process.description: A thirty-minute call to turn a worry into a question research can answer, and to agree what you will do with the answer.

process.title: Find the answer
process.description: We pick the method that fits, whether interviews, a survey, desk research or a mix, and keep you posted every week.

process.title: Say it plainly
process.description: A short readout that starts with the answer, shows the evidence and ends with the decision we would make in your place.

proof.text: They turned a vague worry about pricing into one clear question and then answered it.
The interviews told us why our second purchase rate was low, in our customers' own words.
proof.source: Head of marketing, a skincare start-up (sample)

proof.text: Short readouts, no jargon, and a recommendation at the end.
